paragraphs.text: The mana value of an object is a number determined by the total amount of mana in its mana cost .

"Mana value" was originally known as "casting cost" or "total casting cost" before Sixth Edition . With the Sixth Edition rules changes , "casting cost" became "converted mana cost" (or "CMC" for short). The term "mana value" was introduced in Strixhaven: School of Mages . Thereafter, all cards before this set have their oracle text updated to reflect this change.

The mana value of an object is an integer and is always greater than or equal to zero. Mana value is determined by the sum of the mana symbols in the spell's mana cost . Mana symbols which contain a number, including monocolored hybrid mana symbols ( ), have a value equal to that number. All other mana symbols have a value of 1. Cards without a mana cost, such as lands, have a mana value of 0.

The only case in which a spell's mana value can ever vary is for spells with in the mana cost. When an object with X in the mana cost is on the stack, X equals whatever value was chosen for it when it was put on the stack. In any other zone, X equals 0.

Cards with multiple sets of playable characteristics may have different mana values in different zones, depending on how they were cast or played. Tokens and copies may also have confusing mana values.

Tokens and face-down objects have a mana value of 0 simply because they have no mana cost. Note that a face-down object could turn face-up, at which point it would have its regular attributes rather than a mana value of 0.

The following table shows which number or attribute determines the mana value of an object that is a copy of another object. These rules apply regardless of whether a permanent copy is a token or a non-token card. Generally, if the mana cost can be copied, the mana value is also copied. If the mana value cannot be copied, the mana value of the copy is 0; these are marked with a * below.

Note that a copy of a face-down object cannot turn face-up to regain the original mana value - it will have value 0 regardless of whether the copying object is face-up or face-down. Neither can a copy of a DFC back face nor a melded permanent transform acquire a non-zero mana value, regardless of whether the copying object is itself a DFC, melded, or transformed.

Specialize is designed-for-digital mechanic, the creatures of which gain a mana symbol and its respective color when the Specialize ability is activated. It will register as having increased in mana value.
Several classes of abilities check mana values of cards to determine their effects, most notably when this concept is a theme in a set .
Some cards care about whether the mana value is odd or even .

"Cost matters" was a theme in Scourge ( 16 cards ) that encouraged players to use spells with high mana values. In addition to providing numerous creatures and other spells with mana values 6 or greater, several cards were printed that enhanced or facilitated them. This theme returned as the green-blue mechanic in Commander Legends and as the Prismari mechanic in Strixhaven: School of Mages .

White is the color that most positively interacts with low mana value (anywhere from mana value 3 or less) cards. It can search the library for them and get them back from the graveyard , among other positive interactions.
paragraphs.section: Friendly to low mana value cards

paragraphs.text: Some cards track the amount of mana spent on a spell rather than the mana value, the latter of which is always static. This includes additional and alternative costs. While the technology has been around since Commander 2013 with Marath, Will of the Wild and company, Final Fantasy was the first set to use it as a draft archetype (spending at least four mana on noncreature spells).
